pr.title: Phase 0c2: test projects to .NET 10 and NUnit 5
pr.body:
Phase 0c2 of the modernization: the test solution follows the tools (#7) onto .NET 10.

## What changes

- **RegressionTests, VolumeTests, VMTestRunner.Console** are SDK-style `net10.0-windows` projects. Item lists stay explicit, as in the tools.
- **Package versions** are pinned once, in `hmailserver/test/Directory.Packages.props` (Central Package Management):

  | Package | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | NUnit | 3.13.3 | **5.0.0** |
  | NUnit.ConsoleRunner | 3.15.5 | 3.22.0 (has a `net10.0` agent) |
  | NUnit3TestAdapter | 3.17.0 | 6.3.1 (+ Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk 18.11.0) |
  | NUnit.Analyzers | – | 4.15.0 |
  | NLog | 5.0.1 | 6.2.2 |
  | Newtonsoft.Json | 13.0.3 | 13.0.4 |
  | CommandLineParser | 2.9.1 | 2.9.1 (latest) |
  | PowerShell hosting | Windows PowerShell 5.1 (GAC) | Microsoft.PowerShell.SDK 7.6.8 |
  | System.Management | .NET Framework | 10.0.13 package |

- **The 2,214 classic asserts** (`Assert.IsTrue`, `AreEqual`, `StringAssert`, `CollectionAssert`, …) are rewritten as `Assert.That` with constraints. In NUnit 4 and 5 that is the only built-in assertion model.
  - 20 assertions passed expected and actual in the wrong order; they now put the actual value first.
  - Four `Is.Not.Null.Or.Empty` checks only tested for null. They are now `Is.Not.Null.And.Not.Empty`.
  - Six format-string messages became interpolated strings.
- **The interop** is generated by `Tools/Interop.hMailServer.targets` instead of a `COMReference`. It uses the type library the installed server registered, or falls back to a local server build. The projects therefore also build with `dotnet build`.
- **Code pages:** .NET only ships the Unicode encodings by default. An assembly-wide `[SetUpFixture]` registers `CodePagesEncodingProvider` for the Windows-1252 messages the tests build. `API/Basics.cs`, the only Windows-1252 source file, is now UTF-8.
- **Packages restore into `hmailserver/test/packages/`.** CI and VMTestRunner find `nunit3-console.exe` there.
- **VMTestRunner** now copies the whole test build output to the guest, because a .NET test assembly needs its `.deps.json` and `.runtimeconfig.json` beside it. The guest gets the .NET runtime from the ArzoieMail setup.
- **`tests.yml`:** `nuget restore` is replaced by `msbuild /restore`, and the comments are updated.
- **Obsolete APIs** flagged by the .NET 10 build are replaced: `SHA1CryptoServiceProvider`, the `X509Certificate2` file constructor, and NLog's `Target.Register`.

## Verified locally

- The test solution builds with `dotnet build` and with Visual Studio's MSBuild (`/restore`, Debug and Release). There are no errors, and no warnings beyond the ones already present before this change.
- `nunit3-console --explore` loads `RegressionTests.dll` under the console runner's `net10.0` agent (CLR 10.0.13, NUnit 5.0.0). It discovers **1,294 test cases**, the same total as master's last run: 1,185 passed + 34 inconclusive + 75 skipped.
- Running a fixture without an installed server fails only at `new hMailServer.Application()` with "class not registered". That shows the runner and the interop work on .NET 10.

## Not verified

- **The full regression run** needs an installed server. The `Tests / Regression tests` check on this PR covers it, and should match the 1,185 / 0 / 34 / 75 baseline.
- **VMTestRunner against Hyper-V.** It builds and starts, but this machine has no Hyper-V. It now hosts PowerShell 7 rather than Windows PowerShell 5.1, so `Get-VM`, `Copy-VMFile` and PowerShell Direct need one run on a Hyper-V host.

+<Project>
+  <!-- Settings shared by the projects of hMailServer Tests.sln. -->
+
+  <PropertyGroup>
+    <!-- Packages are restored into hmailserver\test\packages\, where CI and VMTestRunner pick up
+         nunit3-console.exe (packages\nunit.consolerunner\<version>\tools\). -->
+    <RestorePackagesPath>$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)packages\</RestorePackagesPath>
+  </PropertyGroup>
+
+  <PropertyGroup>
+    <!-- The tests run against the installed server, so the interop is generated from the type
+         library that server registered. Without an installed server, it falls back to the type
+         library of a local server build, like the tools. -->
+    <HMailServerTypeLibrary Condition="'$(HMailServerTypeLibrary)' == ''">$([MSBuild]::GetRegistryValueFromView('HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\TypeLib\{DB241B59-A1B1-4C59-98FC-8D101A2995F2}\1.0\0\win64', '', null, RegistryView.Registry64))</HMailServerTypeLibrary>
+  </PropertyGroup>
+</Project>

commit.message:
Move the test projects to .NET 10 and NUnit 5

RegressionTests, VolumeTests and VMTestRunner.Console become SDK-style
net10.0-windows projects, with the item lists kept explicit as in the tools.
Package versions are pinned once, in hmailserver\test\Directory.Packages.props:

  NUnit                 3.13.3 -> 5.0.0
  NUnit.ConsoleRunner   3.15.5 -> 3.22.0 (runs .NET 10 assemblies in its net10.0 agent)
  NUnit3TestAdapter     3.17.0 -> 6.3.1, with Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk 18.11.0
  NUnit.Analyzers       new, 4.15.0
  NLog                  5.0.1  -> 6.2.2
  Newtonsoft.Json       13.0.3 -> 13.0.4
  CommandLineParser     2.9.1 (latest)
  Microsoft.PowerShell.SDK 7.6.8 and System.Management 10.0.13, which replace the
  .NET Framework System.Management(.Automation) references of VMTestRunner.

The 2,214 classic asserts (Assert.IsTrue, AreEqual, ...) and the StringAssert and
CollectionAssert calls are rewritten into the constraint model, Assert.That, which
NUnit 4 and 5 keep as the only built-in model. Assertions where expected and actual
were swapped now name the actual value first, and Is.Not.Null.Or.Empty, which only
checked for null, becomes Is.Not.Null.And.Not.Empty. Format-string messages become
interpolated strings.

The interop is generated by Tools\Interop.hMailServer.targets, from the type library
the installed server registered, instead of a COMReference, so the projects also
build with the dotnet CLI. Without an installed server it falls back to the type
library of a local server build.

.NET only carries the Unicode encodings by default, so an assembly-wide setup fixture
registers the code pages provider for the Windows-1252 messages the tests build.
API\Basics.cs, the only Windows-1252 source file, is now UTF-8.

Packages restore into hmailserver\test\packages\, where CI and VMTestRunner find
nunit3-console.exe. VMTestRunner copies the whole test build output to the guest,
since a .NET test assembly needs its .deps.json, .runtimeconfig.json and
dependencies beside it; the guest gets the .NET runtime from the ArzoieMail setup.

Obsolete APIs the .NET 10 build flags are replaced: SHA1CryptoServiceProvider,
the X509Certificate2 file constructor and NLog's Target.Register.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Keep the test agent alive when a simulated server's client handling fails

The regression run on .NET 10 ended after 31 tests: the NUnit agent exited with
0xE0434352, an unhandled exception.

TcpServer accepted with BeginAcceptSocket and completed with EndAcceptTcpClient.
On .NET Framework the two shared one implementation; on .NET they are task based,
and ending a socket accept as a TcpClient accept throws ArgumentException. The
exception was raised in the thread pool callback, where .NET ends the process,
while the .NET Framework NUnit agent (legacyUnhandledExceptionPolicy) ignored it.

TcpServer now pairs BeginAcceptTcpClient with EndAcceptTcpClient, and logs any
other exception from client handling instead of letting it escape the callback,
as the old agent effectively did. The Send50Messages thread in SMTP\Basics does
the same; a failed send still fails the test through its message count.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
